string.text: Keeps a SortingPlus inventory tidy: when an item lands out of order (gun modified, item moved, traded, marked favorite/junk) it snaps back into its sorted position in place, with no flicker and without losing your scroll position.
Master switch. When off, inventories behave like vanilla SortingPlus (items land at the end until you reopen the window).
Keep your own inventory sorted as you modify, move or pick up items. Turn off to let items land at the end in the inventory screen (and the repair screen) until you reopen it.
Seamless Sort in loot / stash window

Keep both sides sorted while looting bodies, stashes and containers. Turn off to leave the loot screen unsorted as you take and drop items. (The body and Looting Takes Time options on the next page still apply.)
Keep both sale bags sorted while trading. Turn off to leave the trade screen unsorted as you move items in and out of the basket.
When you mark an item favorite or junk (SortingPlus K / J keys or the right-click menu), snap it to the top / bottom instantly in place. When off, SortingPlus' own behavior is used.
Keep modified weapons in the bag

When you attach or detach a scope, silencer or grenade launcher on a weapon in your bag, the engine rebuilds the weapon and equips it to an empty weapon slot, so it jumps out of your bag into the primary / secondary slot. Turn on to move it straight back to the bag so it stays where it was. Turn off to let the engine equip it.
What happens to the empty slots items leave behind. Keep gaps where things were removed, keep the bag perfectly still while you disassemble, and give ammo parts their own group.

When you drop, sell or stash an item and nothing else moved, leave the empty slot where it was instead of repacking everything below it. The gap fills back in next time something is added. Enabled by default in v1.1 to reduce layout work; turn off to repack immediately on removal.
Keep the bag still when disassembling

While you disassemble, nothing in the bag moves: the dismantled item's slot stays empty and the resulting parts land at the end, so disassembling in quick succession never makes the inventory jump. When you stop, a single re-sort folds the parts into their group and closes the gaps -- the slider below sets how long it waits. Works on its own -- it does not need "Keep gaps after removing items".

How long after your last disassembly the bag waits before the settle re-sort. 0 re-sorts the moment the parts land; higher values keep the bag still through a whole disassembly session. Each disassembly restarts the timer. Default 0 s (re-sort as soon as the parts land).

Sort casings, bullets and gunpowder (Ammo Maker parts) into their own group right below the ammo instead of mixing them in between the ammo boxes. Takes effect the next time a bag is sorted (reopen the inventory).

Where the ammo parts category sits in the overall sort order, on SortingPlus' scale where ammo is 9 and mutant parts are 10. Default 9.5 puts ammo parts right below the ammo. Lower moves them up (toward weapons and armor), higher moves them down (toward food and junk). Only matters when "Own category for ammo parts" is on. Takes effect on the next sort (reopen the inventory).
How looted dead bodies are handled. Only dead bodies are affected on this page; stashes, containers and your own inventory always sort.

What to do with a looted dead body's items. Only dead bodies are affected; stashes, containers, companions and your own bag always sort.

- Sort normally: sort the body like any container.
- Never sort - keep as found: leave the body unsorted (size-kind layout), the same as SortingPlus' "sort npc inventories" off, but for corpses only. No Looting Takes Time needed.
- Keep Looting Takes Time order: never sort; leave the body exactly in the order Looting Takes Time revealed it. (Looting Takes Time only; behaves like "Sort normally" without it.)
- Sort after Looting Takes Time reveal: wait for the reveal to finish, then sort once and keep it sorted as you loot. (Looting Takes Time only.)
Sort after Looting Takes Time reveal
Tint items you just took from a container, stash or body with a colored background, so you can see at a glance what you found. The highlight clears when you close the inventory.
Enable the new-loot highlight. Use the sliders below to choose the color.
Red component of the highlight color (0-255).
Green component of the highlight color (0-255).
Blue component of the highlight color (0-255).
Opacity of the highlight (0-255). Low values give a subtle tint; high values a strong, solid color. Default 60.

Splits initial sorting and icon creation for a large inventory across multiple frames. The adaptation only affects the actor bag, loot/container bag and two sale bags; every other UI container keeps the original code path.
Large containers open without one blocking sort. Small containers always use the original immediate path.

Enables multi-frame loading for actor_trade_bag and npc_trade_bag. Keep disabled for the diagnostic test: trade lists use the original engine path while Antifreeze remains active in normal inventory and corpse-loot grids. Close and reopen the trade window after changing this option.
Containers below this count are not intercepted. Recommended: 120-200. Lower values engage deferred loading more often.
Maximum time Antifreeze attempts to spend in one UI frame. 1-2 ms is smoothest; higher values fill the window faster but affect frametime more.
Secondary safety cap. Actual work is also limited by the millisecond budget.
Lower is smoother but fills the window more slowly. Recommended: 8-16.
Shows a spinner while a large list is built. Disabled by default to minimize rendering and texture-memory overhead.
Catches an unstable sort-key error and uses a deterministic fallback instead of crashing. Recommended.

Batch sorting merges a burst of purchases, transfers or pickups into one final layout pass. Timers sleep until work is due instead of polling every frame. Trade has a separate policy and a safety limit for very large sale bags.
- Instant: v1.0 behaviour, sort after every change.\n- Balanced: short delay and one sort per operation burst. Recommended.\n- Maximum FPS: longer delays for trade and large inventories.

Full: re-sort both sale bags after all changes. Additions only: recommended; sort only the side that received items and leave a gap on the side items were removed from. Off: no live seamless sorting in trade, for maximum smoothness with very large traders.
When one sale bag contains more items than this limit, the addon leaves it unsorted while the trade window is open to avoid a heavy single-frame hitch. 0 disables the limit. Recommended: 300.
Back off from re-sorting a container that is churning. Leave on unless troubleshooting.
How many re-sorts of one container within a one-second window are allowed before the guard decides it is oscillating. Lower = more aggressive. Default 8.
How long the guard stops re-sorting an oscillating container so it can settle, then seamless sorting resumes. Default 1.5 s.

This diagnostic build measures active trade UI methods and writes compact reports to the xray log. Timing format: calls / total ms / average ms / maximum ms. Fast highlight cleanup replaces the stock every-frame full inventory scan with a sparse set of cells that were actually highlighted.
Collects counters and timings only while trade UI is open. Keep enabled for this test build.
How often a periodic REPORT is written to the log. Five seconds is recommended.
Writes a rate-limited SLOW line when a measured phase exceeds this threshold.

In trade mode, processes only cells that were actually highlighted instead of scanning every actor and trader item on every idle frame. Disable and report the exact scenario if a highlight remains stuck.
